8.0.s.en: (1) The opening of the seventh seal and the golden censer

8.0.0.en: When the seventh seal was opened, silence reigned in all of heaven. The silence here points to readiness and anticipation for the occurrence of something new, great and awesome.

8.0.1.en: "Half an hour" is a period of time that is not measured by earthly time, but the Fathers agreed that its mention is a figure for the shortness of this quiet period.

8.0.2.en: "The seven angels" are the seven archangels, of whom the angel Raphael said in the Book of Tobit that he is one.

8.0.3.en: "Were given" means that they were charged by God to carry the trumpets and sound them to proclaim His successive warnings to mankind as a result of their lack of repentance.

8.0.4.en: The trumpet: trumpets were a familiar sight in Jewish worship and were also used by the pagan peoples. Their most important uses were:

8.0.5.en: 1- Announcing the beginning of religious celebrations.

8.0.6.en: 2- Preparing for war, whether in defense or attack.

8.0.7.en: 3- A warning of the working of God's power, as happened when the walls of Jericho fell after the blowing of the trumpets.

8.1.0.en: Another angel: that is, not one of the seven archangels who carry the trumpets, but one who has a mission of intercession and supplication, as we shall see.

8.1.1.en: A golden censer ... a golden altar: since this angel stood before the divine throne and in the face of God Himself, the censer and likewise the altar could only be of pure gold, as a reference to the splendor of God's glory and to the fact that everything that stands before God is not defective or flawed.

8.1.2.en: The mission of this angel is to offer much incense, that is, fervent intercessory prayers, which were accompanied also by the intercessory prayers of the heavenly saints on behalf of the believers on earth. This heavenly scene confirms the belief of our Church in the intercession of the angels and saints, offered on our behalf at all times before the throne of God. In another symbolic interpretation: some saw that this "angel" is the Lord Jesus Himself, who stood before the altar (the Cross) carrying the golden censer (His sufferings and His atoning intercession), and the Father accepted it and accepted with it also the intercessions of the saints and their petitions.

8.2.0.en: After the angel offered the incense, he took from the fire of the altar, which represents divine justice, and cast it upon the earth, and frightening things happened, such as thunders, lightnings and earthquakes, to alert people and warn them before the proclamation of "the warning trumpets."

8.2.1.en: My beloved brother, God in His love for us and the breadth of His heart accepts on our behalf the prayers and intercessions of the angels and saints, and He is longsuffering and slow to anger, so He does not bring upon the wicked the punishment they deserve all at once, but warns and cautions repeatedly ... But we must not forget that He is also a just and awesome God ... So do not neglect your repentance or postpone it, and take for yourself an intercessor, a friend, who supports you with his prayers before the throne of grace.

8.3.0.en: Prepared themselves: that is, got ready without haste, as a reference to God's patience with mankind, that perhaps they would repent.

8.3.1.en: Hail and fire: they remind us of God's plague upon Pharaoh in (Ex 9:23), "the Lord gave hail, and fire ran along upon the ground." The use of a noun and its opposite (hail and fire) means the breadth of the punishment and its inclusion of all degrees, as when we say "right and left" and mean all places, or we say "sweet and bitter" and mean all foods. The meaning here is that whoever escapes the "hail" and bears it is harmed by the fire, and whoever is not affected by the intensity of the heat is destroyed and killed by the hail. Mingled with blood: how can fire be mingled with hail and with blood?! These are frightening expressions that the Holy Spirit used to proclaim the divine wrath upon mankind if they do not repent.

8.3.2.en: A third part: that is, despite the just wrath of God, He does not bring upon us exactly what we deserve. His wide mercy made this punishment a third, because the purpose of these warnings is the repentance of man and his return, not the final divine retribution.

8.3.3.en: The trees and all green grass: that is, the first warning is directed to the agricultural and food goods of the earth, which represent the most important needs of man for life on earth.

8.3.4.en: When a material tribulation meets you or your needs fall short in anything, do not be disturbed, but accept it with contentment and examine yourself. Perhaps God intends that you notice a fault in you that you should correct, or something lacking that you should complete. He loves you and seeks the salvation of your soul, even if He allows a limited material hardship for you.

8.4.0.en: A great mountain burning with fire: that is, a tyrannical ruler or a great state that stirs up war (the same comparison God used in speaking of the king of Babylon in (Jer 51:25)). Was cast into the sea: the sea, in its vastness and the turbulence of its waves, points to the world in upheaval. The meaning is that the second warning is a warning of a great war that sweeps over the world in all its regions, like the world wars, and the cause of it will be the pride of a great nation, like the burning mountain. The results of this war will be: the third part of the sea became blood: that is, the death resulting from the fighting and people's destroying one another includes a third of the inhabitants of the earth, or a third of all "creatures which had life," for deadly weapons take man and animal together. The third part of the ships: the destruction of a third of the ships points to the severing of ties and communication between people, on the one hand because of the horror of the war and its results, or on the other hand because each person is occupied with his own selfishness to the exclusion of others. The whole picture is very frightening, for the word "third" here means millions of people, and death may include one person from every family. War is a human creation, the result of man's evil, although God allows it, perhaps so that it may be a severe warning for his turning back from his evil.

8.4.1.en: Whatever your position or authority, do not use it for your own benefit at the expense of others, harming them so that you may profit. Rather, make peace and love as much as you can, so that you will have a treasure in heaven to rejoice in.

8.5.0.en: When the third angel sounded, he announced to us a new problem that becomes a cause of the destruction of many.

8.5.1.en: The fall of a great star: that is, a religious leadership of standing, or a spiritual leadership that used to shine with its teachings like a lamp. But when it fell, teachings foreign to the faith came upon a third of the rivers and the springs. The rivers and the springs: these are what people quench their thirst from and drink from, and the meaning is that because of the spread of a faith foreign to the right faith of the Church, thoughts (the rivers) and feelings (the springs) became completely polluted.

8.5.2.en: The name of the star is Wormwood: wormwood is an extremely bitter herb, and this name is used as a figure for the intense bitterness of teaching foreign to the faith, for it is deadly to everyone who tastes it. It can also be said how bitter it is to the heart of God that those who were once enlightened by the sound faith should perish, then deviate and fall after the one who led them astray by his fall.

8.5.3.en: A third part of the waters: as we pointed out before, the third means that many went astray, but God in His mercies and care still keeps the remainder in their sound faith.

8.5.4.en: God entrusted the deposit of the faith to His pure Apostles and His holy Church, and our Fathers kept it for us by the tradition handed down to us with their blood ... So take refuge, beloved, in the Church and her Fathers, and do not accept bitter, destructive teaching, even if it seems sweet and smooth, so long as it is foreign to your Church and your ears have not been accustomed to it before.

8.6.0.en: A third part of the sun: our sun is our Christ.

8.6.1.en: A third part of the moon: the moon is the Church, which reflects the light of her Christ and so lights the darkness of hearts.

8.6.2.en: A third part of the stars: they are the men of God and the spiritual leaders who shine in His Church like stars. A new warning and caution comes with the fourth trumpet, for with the increase of heresies and errors, a third of the sun is struck, that is, people transgress against the Lord Christ either by denying His divinity or by not confessing Him at all, through their atheism and turning away from Him.

8.6.3.en: Likewise many reject the authority of their mother the Church (the moon) and so deprive themselves of her lights, and this darkness also includes many of the clergy (the stars), so a third of them fall, their light vanishes, and they lose the splendor of their example for the believers.

8.6.4.en: The day shone not for a third part of it, and the night likewise: that is, the darkness of evil entered the day and the night, which signifies evil, and it became more evil and more dark.

8.7.0.en: "An angel flying through the midst of heaven": he is not one of the seven archangels holding the trumpets, but this scene separates the first four trumpets from the remaining three. For this reason some of the Fathers see that this angel is the Holy Spirit Himself, who warns of what is to come.

8.7.1.en: With a loud voice: a voice of majesty and awe.

8.7.2.en: Woe, woe, woe to the inhabiters of the earth: frightening words that announce that what is to come is far worse in its terrors than what has gone before ...

8.7.3.en: Save us, O God our Savior, from the hard times and keep us in Your name, for we have no other besides You whom we hope in and for whose fatherly mercies we wait ... As long as You are with us we fear no evil, for You keep us, whatever the tribulations around us.

8.7.4.en: The fifth and sixth trumpets, introduction to chapter nine: the previous chapter contained the first four warnings and ended with a strongly worded proclamation of what is coming in the following trumpets, and for this reason the next three trumpets are called the woes, because of the terrors they contain.

9.0.s.en: (1) The fifth trumpet (the opening of the abyss)

9.0.0.en: A star fallen: either an angel sent on assignment by God to open the gates of Hades, or it is Satan himself, given the same authority by God's permission. Perhaps this is the more probable, and it agrees with the expression "fallen," for we know that Satan was one of the archangels but fell through his pride and did not abide in the love of God.

9.0.1.en: To him was given the key: that is, he came to have authority to bring out his helpers, the demons, to war against all mankind, but within the limits of God's permission.

9.1.0.en: He indeed opened the pit of the abyss, and as soon as he opened it a dense smoke came out that caused people to lose right vision.

9.1.1.en: A furnace: a burning, intensely blazing oven.

9.1.2.en: Smoke: these are the doubting thoughts of Satan and the wars of atheism, which by their density made people lose sight of the Lord Christ (the Sun of righteousness), and thick darkness wrapped them, that is, the sound faith was lost.

9.2.0.en: There came out locusts: of course the locusts here are the demons, and when God pictures them to us in the form of locusts, it is so that we may know:

9.2.1.en: First: their great number; for the locust is an insect whose swarms are estimated at hundreds of millions when they attack. Second: the severity of their destruction; for the locust eats everything it meets on its way and leaves the land only bare. Unto them was given power: that is, Satan has no power over mankind unless it is permitted to him by God and within the limits of the discipline that He sees fit.

9.2.2.en: As the scorpions of the earth have power: the scorpion's sting to a man is very painful and its poison penetrating, and the use of the comparison of scorpions together with locusts is only an addition to the severity of this woe that comes upon the world.

9.3.0.en: It was commanded them: that is, it was commanded by God, who determines the size, measure and kind of the discipline by His absolute authority.

9.3.1.en: The grass ... any tree: the grass signifies the little ones among the believers ... and the tree those of higher stature in the faith. The general meaning is that although God allowed Satan this blow, He prevented him from approaching the believers of all their degrees, for God, in His tenderness and love for His children, protects the weak and the strong among them from the deceptions of Satan and does not allow him to influence them or to affect them.

9.3.2.en: Which have not the seal of God: this woe strikes the people who do not have the mark of the Holy Spirit on their foreheads, and they are of two kinds. The first is the one who was not baptized and so never received the mark at all, or one who was a Christian but, because of his constant refusal of repentance, quenched and grieved the Spirit, so that Satan gained authority over him.

9.4.0.en: The mercy of God appears in His not allowing harm to the point of death (killing), but only for five months, which is a period of the proclamation of God's wrath on mankind, as happened in the days of the Flood (Gen 7:24), when the waters increased for five months.

9.4.1.en: As for the degree of discipline, it is very severe, which the Holy Scripture likened to us as pain resulting from the sting of a scorpion that runs through a person's veins, and he finds no remedy for his pain.

9.5.0.en: Continuing the description of the severity of people's pain from the force of the divine discipline: they wish for death to escape what has come upon them, but even death they do not obtain, and their torment continues, perhaps that they may repent.

9.5.1.en: We thank You, our tender God, for You had pity on the weakness of our faith and did not leave Satan any authority over us that would destroy our faith ... but You strengthened us and gave us an opportunity for repentance. And the punishment You allowed for others is a warning to us, so that our attachment to You may increase ... for You alone are our help, our salvation and our goal.

9.6.s.en: (2) The features of the war in this woe

9.6.0.en: Among the pictures of God's love for His children is that He reveals to them the features and attributes of the enemy warrior so that they may prepare and not be deceived by him ... These declared attributes are nine in number and carry many spiritual meanings and symbols.

9.6.1.en: 1- The shapes of the locusts were like unto horses prepared unto battle: the horse is the strongest and swiftest of the animals used in war, and the word "prepared" means that they will use all their strength, as though they had made ready and trained to bring man down.

9.6.2.en: 2- On their heads were as it were crowns like gold: that is, they have authority and standing over people like the kings who wear golden crowns, but it is counterfeit gold by which the children of God are not deceived, because it is only like gold. It may also be a reference to material wars, the love of luxury and the grandeur of living, which entice and seduce many people.

9.6.3.en: 3- Their faces were as the faces of men: that is, Satan uses helpers from among human beings who have accepted his thought and become soldiers for him, promoting him and persuading others of his evils.

9.7.0.en: 4- They had hair as the hair of women: that is, Satan in his wars uses every means, even the soft and alluring ones (like women).

9.7.1.en: 5- Their teeth were as the teeth of lions: that is, although softness is the outward appearance of Satan's wars, ferocity and devouring are his inner reality.

9.8.0.en: 6- They had breastplates: breastplates of iron, that is, a symbol of hardness and severity in fighting.

9.8.1.en: 7- Their wings: that is, the wings of the locusts (the demons) make a terrifying and disturbing sound, like the sound of war chariots which, in their number and multitude, spread terror in people's souls.

9.9.0.en: 8- They had tails like unto scorpions: curved and poisonous. The tail is the end of the matter, so even if these demons have a crown like gold, a human face and soft hair, the end is the sting with poison.

9.9.1.en: 9- In their tails were stings: the burning heat (hummā) is intense embers of fire, and this expression is a figure for Satan's poison, which runs through the body like grains of blazing fire, so that the deceived person who is stung by them has severe pain.

9.9.2.en: Five months: that is, a limited period that symbolizes God's wrath; see (v. 5).

9.10.0.en: The angel of the abyss: that is, the chief of all the demons (the devil), who directs these wars and guides his soldiers to destroy man and cause him to lose his salvation in Christ.

9.10.1.en: His name is "Abaddon" or "Apollyon": a word whose meaning is "the Destroyer." It was mentioned in the two languages known at that time because of the importance of proclaiming his name and his attribute to everyone, so that people may guard against his thoughts ... and his deception and discover his true aim of destruction.

9.11.0.en: One woe: this was the first of the woes, and it is what the fifth trumpet carries, while the two other woes to come are those carried by the sixth and seventh trumpets.

9.11.1.en: Take heed, my brother, that the wars of the demons mostly take the appearance of softness and pleasure at their beginning until they make you fall, but inside them are poison, pain and burning fire, then destruction. So do not accept his lusts, however alluring they are, and if you fall, rise quickly with repentance and tears, for your God loves you and rescues you from his hand.

9.12.s.en: (3) The sixth trumpet and the second woe

9.12.0.en: The golden altar: this is the same altar before which the angel offered incense in (ch. 8:3), and from whose fire he also took and cast it from the altar upon the earth, so that there were great warnings (ch. 8:5). Four horns: that is, the four corners of the altar, for the altar had horns on its corners. This is the picture of the altar familiar among the Jews in their worship, whether in the tabernacle of meeting or in Solomon's temple afterward. When the sixth angel sounded, the voice came from the four horns at one time, as a reference to its strength and severity on the one hand, and to its universality and its reaching the whole inhabited world on the other.

9.13.0.en: This voice was a divine command to the sixth angel himself to release and give authority to four angels who were bound.

9.13.1.en: The four angels which are bound: some see that they are angels who had been charged by God with carrying out what is to come upon the world in this woe, and this charge was postponed until the command is given at the sixth trumpet to loose them from their bonds. Some see that they are four demons of formidable power who have been bound since the fall of man, and God will now leave them, by His permission, to come upon the earth with evils and wars in fulfillment of the second woe!! Whether they were this or that, it will not change anything in reality, since everything happens by the command and permission of God and in fulfillment of His will.

9.13.2.en: In the great river Euphrates: the river Euphrates passed through the kingdom of Babylon, which was always a symbol in the Holy Bible of the kingdom of evil, and this means that these angels who carry out the second woe bear a severe punishment.

9.14.0.en: For an hour, and a day, and a month, and a year: that is, everything under heaven has a time by a precise divine plan, so nothing is before or after its appointed time, even by one minute. The purpose of this verse is to bring out a part of the divine wisdom and the attribute of God as "the Controller of all."

9.14.1.en: The third part of men: punishment by a third was constantly repeated in chapter eight, and the meaning here and there is one. In His justice God allows punishment and retribution upon the wicked, and in His mercy He makes this punishment not destroy everyone but the lesser part, and calls the greater part (the two thirds) to return, repent and enjoy His mercies.

9.15.0.en: The number of the warriors in this woe is two hundred million, and the expression "I heard the number of them" means that God willed for us, through the Saint, to know the number, which is a vast and enormous number. The purpose of mentioning it is to know the severity and power of this woe and its devastating results ... The exact number mentioned is not what is meant, but it signifies that their number is very great.

9.15.1.en: We believers must not be terrified by the frightening and continuous wars of the demons, but must fortify ourselves with God's promises to His children, for no one can take us from His hand or touch us with harm, because those who are with us are always more than those who are against us ... God's promises are true, and all who love His holy name rely on them until He fulfills for us the proclamation of salvation at His glorious Second Coming ... Amen.

9.16.s.en: (4) The force of the blow, and the refusal of repentance

9.16.0.en: St. John begins to explain the scene of the armies and sees in it the following:

9.16.1.en: The horses and them that sat on them: the rider's sitting on the steed means the state of final readiness to enter the war.

9.16.2.en: Breastplates of fire: that is, the war is burning, without mercy or respite.

9.16.3.en: Jacinth: blue, having the color of the sky. The meaning is either that they come in the appearance of the heavenly beings to deceive people, or that the color of the sky means, in the view of some, the divine permission of this war.

9.16.4.en: Brimstone: a symbol of the divine wrath, which when it burned Sodom and Gomorrah burned them with fire and brimstone (Gen 19:24). The heads of lions: the head of the horse is of a gentle appearance, and for this reason St. John saw it in a more terrifying, devouring and destructive appearance, as they became the heads of lions.

9.16.5.en: Fire and smoke and brimstone: they refer to the hosts of the demons in their nature and in what they cause to others during their war.

9.17.0.en: By these three (the fire, the smoke and the brimstone): that is, by what the demons stir up. The forces of evil, with their various weapons (v. 17), were able to destroy a great number of people, but the mercies of God preserved the two thirds, perhaps that those who remain may understand, return and repent.

9.18.0.en: Their power is in their mouth: that is, their false, honeyed speech.

9.18.1.en: Their tails: their tails are like the tails of poisonous scorpions.

9.18.2.en: This scene pictures and explains to us where the strength of Satan lies. It is first in his mouth and his deceptive speech, and it was the first weapon he used against man when by his lie he brought down Adam and Eve (Gen 3:5). His strength lies also in his tails, which carry the poisons of lusts, so that if he stings with them an incautious person, lust possesses him and becomes in his veins like deadly poison until he dies and perishes spiritually. He fights man from every direction and with many kinds of wars.

9.18.3.en: Their tails had heads: this means that before Satan stings man with these lusts and sins, he first uses logic (the heads) to persuade the man, to justify the sin and to make him doubt the punishment and judgment, so that he slips into it, overcome and obedient to it.

9.19.0.en: And the rest of the men: that is, the two thirds who escaped this woe, instead of repenting and returning, became more deviant, so Satan and evil possessed them in various forms.

9.19.1.en: Gold and silver: that is, people worshipped and craved wealth, riches and material luxury, which is one of the forms of the worship of Satan.

9.19.2.en: Brass and stone and wood: that is, possessions, houses, palaces and material luxury. What is meant here is people's turning away from God and being occupied with the perishing things of earth rather than the heavenly things. And God shows us, in a gentle rebuking manner, that all of them are things without benefit and without life, for they neither see nor hear, and they remind us of what God said to us before: "They have forsaken Me, the fountain of living waters, and hewed them out cisterns, broken cisterns, that can hold no water" (Jer 2:13).

9.20.0.en: People continued in their evil and did not repent, nor did they benefit from the woe of the sixth trumpet, but continued in all their sins, such as adultery, theft and others. This means that most of the living people deviated from God, and those who still keep their faith and pure conduct are few, so that the general scene of mankind is distance from God.

9.20.1.en: My God ... Satan is very cruel in his wars and in his destruction of mankind ... but what terrifies me here is the hardness of my heart and its failure to realize what is going on around it and what is happening to it, so that it does not understand the evil that befalls it, but increases in deviation and in straying after Satan and his deception ... I beg You, my God, rescue us from this evil enemy and from our weaknesses and from every lust and uncleanness that separates us from Your goodness, O Lover of mankind.

9.20.2.en: The angel clothed with a cloud and the open book, introduction to chapter ten: after the sixth trumpet (ch. 9) and before the seventh trumpet (ch. 11:15), we find that the Book of Revelation presents us with two interjected visions. The first, which comprises "chapter ten," has as its subject the appearance of a mighty angel and a reference to thunders uttered beforehand, while the second vision concerns the appearance of the two witnesses (ch. 11:1-14). Each of these visions has its significances and meanings, and after them we return to the next trumpet, as we mentioned.
